output_list.reason: The transferProxy function is vulnerable to reentrancy attacks. It allows the sender to transfer tokens to another address and also transfer a fee in SMT tokens. However, the function does not check if the recipient contract has implemented the receiveApproval function before transferring the tokens. This could allow the recipient contract to call the transferProxy function again, leading to a reentrancy attack.

The approveProxy function is vulnerable to reentrancy attacks. It allows the sender to approve a spender to transfer tokens on behalf of the sender. However, the function does not check if the recipient contract has implemented the receiveApproval function before approving the spender. This could allow the recipient contract to call the approveProxy function again, leading to a reentrancy attack.

The allocateTokens function is vulnerable to integer overflow attacks. It allows the owner to allocate tokens to multiple addresses. However, the function does not check if the total supply will overflow before adding the new tokens to the total supply. This could allow the total supply to exceed the maximum value for uint256, leading to an integer overflow.
